Entries.Text: Find map objects, then edit or delete all of them at once. The edit is shown before it is applied.
Choose the map objects to edit.
Choose what to do to the map objects found, see what it will do, and apply it.
The map objects to look through.
The parts, regions and events that are selected.
Every map of the project. Maps that aren't loaded are read for the find, and an edit to them is written straight to the project, which can't be undone.
Select some parts, regions or events to find among them.
Conditions on the fields of the map objects. Every condition must be met. A condition with only a field finds the objects that have that field.
Add a condition on a field.
Find the map objects. Find with nothing filled in finds every object in the scope.
Find the map objects that match the inputs above.
Clear the inputs and the matches.
The map objects found. Click one to select it, loading its map first if needed.
The inputs or the selection have changed since Find. Press Find again before applying anything.
Find some map objects in the Find tab first.
What to do to the map objects found.
The changes to make, applied in order to each map object. An object is changed by every step or, if any can't apply to it, by none.
The field to change. The list holds the fields of the map objects found; Name can't be changed, as other objects refer to them by it.
The value to use. Whole numbers are rounded, and a result outside the field's range leaves the object alone.
One number applies to every component; one number per component, split by commas, applies to each in turn (0, 3, 0 adds 3 to Y).
The range a random number is drawn from, both ends included. For a vector, a number is drawn for each component.
Every occurrence of the first text is replaced with the second, matching case.
Set the field to the value.
Add the value to the field.
Subtract the value from the field.
Multiply the field by the factor.
Divide the field by the factor.
Raise the field to the value if it is below it.
Lower the field to the value if it is above it.
Set the field to a random number in the range. The numbers are drawn when the changes are worked out, so the preview shows what is applied.
Add a random number in the range to the field, such as -1 and 1 to scatter positions. The numbers are drawn when the changes are worked out, so the preview shows what is applied.
Turn the field on if it is off, and off if it is on.
Put the text in front of the field.
Put the text after the field.
Replace a text within the field with another.
The operator can't be used on a {0}
'{0}' isn't one number or {1} numbers split by commas
'{0}' to '{1}' isn't a range of numbers
The result is outside the range of a {0}
Replace needs a text to find
What the steps will do: each field that changes, from its value now to its new value. Click one to select its map object.
Pick a field for a step to see what it will change.
{0} changes to {1} map objects in {2} maps.
{0} map objects already have these values.
The inputs or the selection have changed since Find. Press Find again to apply.
{0} of the maps aren't loaded. They are written straight to the project, which can't be undone. Edits to loaded maps can be undone, and are kept until the maps are saved.
Make the changes listed. The changes to loaded maps are one action, so a single undo takes them back.
Delete the map objects found. Fields of other objects that refer to them are left pointing at nothing.
Delete the map objects found. The deletions in loaded maps are one action, so a single undo puts them back.
{0} maps aren't loaded, and will be written straight to the project. This can't be undone:
{0} map objects were left alone, as they had changed since Find or were gone.
{0} map objects were left alone, as their map is loaded in another view.
Wrote {0} maps that aren't loaded to the project.
Map {0} was left as it was: {1}
Save the loaded maps to keep their changes.
Press Find again to make another edit.
MSB mass edit: {0} map objects applied, {1} stale, {2} unloaded maps written, {3} failed.
